parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for a full parse-compatible API, type conversions, datetime handling, Result and Parser behavior, examples, installability, and strong behavioral parity with parse 1.20.2.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Kept implementation ownership in the parent actor. It announced a later fan-out plan, but the observable execution before timeout created only task tracker records and no child-agent work.
parallel.implementation: Wrote a large single-file parse.py, built black-box differential drivers, fixed anonymous-index, datetime, and extract_format divergences, and reached zero differences on core and API-surface probes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered only parse.py plus bytecode in the artifact; the planned packaging and larger fuzz/scaffolding tasks were not executed before timeout.
parallel.verification: Ran reference-oracle comparisons with 0/14185 core observation differences, 0/473 datetime probe differences, and 0/393 API-surface differences before creating tracker tasks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out with an empty final response, no executed child results, and no visible packaging/docs in the artifact, though the official evaluator still passed the code at 96/96.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same parse-compatible API, project scaffolding, reference test behavior, installability, README examples, and broad matching/conversion semantics.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as one serial owner with workflows disabled, first studying reference tests and implementation details, then implementing, packaging, and verifying locally.
serial.implementation: Wrote parse.py, corrected timezone behavior, added pyproject.toml, README.rst, LICENSE, .pytest.ini, .gitignore, .git-blame-ignore-revs, and produced install/build metadata.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated source and packaging into a coherent final workspace artifact that included source, metadata, docs, license/config files, egg-info, and build output.
serial.verification: Ran the copied official tests with 96 passed and 1 skipped, README doctests, pip installability checks, a deterministic differential script with zero diffs, and randomized fuzz with zero diffs.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Also timed out with an empty final response, but its artifact was complete enough for packaging and official evaluation, and no unresolved official-test defect remained.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode actor understood the required Parse APIs, converters, parser classes, version, and examples and focused on matching parse 1.20.2 behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor understood the same requirements and additionally carried through the prompt's complete-project packaging and documentation requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both satisfied the official tests, but the serial artifact covered more of the prompt's non-source project-file surface while parallel delivered mainly parse.py.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned the work directly until the very end, where it created two task-tracker items rather than executed child agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation by design and kept implementation, packaging, and verification under one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no operative multi-agent decomposition in either mode; the only parallel-specific artifact was late task tracking without child execution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child brief, cross-agent contract, child handoff, or retry state existed; all task knowledge stayed in the parent-local trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise had no child interfaces, and its control configuration explicitly disabled workflow and task delegation tools.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no context-transfer boundary to compare; interface differences are ordinary artifact-scope differences, not parallel coordination defects.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote parse.py first, then iteratively differential-tested and edited parsing, datetime, and formatting behavior against a reference oracle.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial studied official tests and reference source, wrote parse.py, made a timezone fix, then created the surrounding project files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced a passing parser; serial leaned on official/reference tests earlier and packaged the project, while parallel emphasized custom differential harnesses and left packaging unexecuted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child result lifecycle existed. The two late TaskCreate calls returned task IDs only and no child outputs were ever joined before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and no delegated outputs to join, so all results were local command outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel has no retrievable child work to inspect or lose; the task tracker records did not change the final artifact before official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final copied artifact for parallel contained only parse.py and its bytecode, with no observed concurrent writers or shared workspace conflicts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial final artifact contained parse.py plus pyproject, README, license/config files, egg-info, bytecode, and build/lib/parse.py.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial integrated the package-level project surface more completely, while parallel's artifact remained source-only; no shared-state collision explains that difference.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed extensive black-box checks and reached zero observed differences on core, datetime probe, full core rerun, and API-surface comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran official copied tests, README doctests, installability checks, deterministic differential tests, and randomized fuzzing, all with passing or zero-diff results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong verification and both passed official evaluation; serial verification additionally covered packaging and docs while parallel verification centered on parse.py behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after about 2401 seconds with return code 143, after creating late tracker tasks but before executing them or writing a final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out near the same budget with return code 143 and no final response, but after finishing a broader artifact and verification sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed through timeout and both passed; parallel's unfinished tracker tasks did not produce a failed official outcome, and without executed children they cannot support a concurrency label.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_pass, not discordant: current completed evaluations in status.json report 96/96 for both parallel and serial. The meaningful process contrast is that serial produced a more complete project scaffold and more package-oriented verification, while the parallel-mode run delivered only parse.py plus bytecode but still passed the official tests. The parallel run did not actually use a child-agent mechanism, so no parallel coordination pattern can be retained.
parallel_contributors: Implemented parse.py and repaired behavioral divergences until core and API-surface differential checks reached zero differences.
Did not execute child agents; late TaskCreate entries were task-tracker records only.
serial_contributors: Implemented parse.py, generated package/docs/config files, and ran official tests, doctests, install checks, and differential fuzzing.
Remained a valid serial control with workflows disabled and no delegation observed.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial produced package scaffolding and documentation files that parallel left absent from the copied artifact.
Parallel spent more work on custom differential API drivers before creating unexecuted follow-up task records.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator appears to grade the parse behavior strongly enough that parallel's missing packaging/docs did not change the pass result.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; process differences are descriptive and do not establish a parallel coordination failure
